FOREWORD TO THE FOURTH

1

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: I have long been conscious of the fact that this book, which was written thirty-seven years ago, stood in urgent need of revision, but my professional obligations and my scientific work never left me sufficient leisure to settle down in comfort to this unpleasant and difficult task.
text_raw:
I have long been conscious of the fact that this book, which
was written thirty-seven years ago, stood in urgent need of
revision, but my professional obligations and my scientific
work never left me sufficient leisure to settle down in comfort
to this unpleasant and difficult task.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: Old age and illness released me at last from my professional duties and gave me the necessary time to contemplate the sins of my youth.
text_raw:
Old age and illness
released me at last from my professional duties and gave me
the necessary time to contemplate the sins of my youth.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: I have never felt happy about this book, much less satisfied with it: it was written at top speed, amid the rush and press of my medical practice, without regard to time or method.
text_raw:
I have
never felt happy about this book, much less satisfied with it: it
was written at top speed, amid the rush and press of my
medical practice, without regard to time or method.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: I had to fling my material hastily together, just as I found it.
text_raw:
I had to
fling my material hastily together, just as I found it.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: There was no opportunity to let my thoughts mature.
text_raw:
There
was no opportunity to let my thoughts mature.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: The whole thing came upon me like a landslide that cannot be stopped.
text_raw:
The whole
thing came upon me like a landslide that cannot be stopped.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: The urgency that lay behind it became clear to me only later: it was the explosion of all those psychic contents which could find no room, no breathing-space, in the constricting atmosphere of Freudian psychology and its narrow outlook.
text_raw:
The urgency that lay behind it became clear to me only later:
it was the explosion of all those psychic contents which could
find no room, no breathing-space, in the constricting
atmosphere of Freudian psychology and its narrow outlook.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: I have no wish to denigrate Freud, or to detract from the extraordinary merits of his investigation of the individual psyche.
text_raw:
I
have no wish to denigrate Freud, or to detract from the
extraordinary merits of his investigation of the individual
psyche.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: But the conceptual framework into which he fitted the psychic phenomenon seemed to me unendurably narrow.
text_raw:
But the conceptual framework into which he fitted the
psychic phenomenon seemed to me unendurably narrow.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: I am not thinking here of his theory of neurosis, which can be as narrow as it pleases if only it is adequate to the empirical facts, or of his theory of dreams, about which different views may be held in all good faith;
text_raw:
I am
not thinking here of his theory of neurosis, which can be as
narrow as it pleases if only it is adequate to the empirical
facts, or of his theory of dreams, about which different views
may be held in all good faith;

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: I am thinking more of the reductive causalism of his whole outlook, and the almost
text_raw:
I am thinking more of the
reductive causalism of his whole outlook, and the almost

chapter_title: Frontmatter
Frontmatter
text: complete disregard of the teleological directedness which is so characteristic of everything psychic.
text_raw:
complete disregard of the teleological directedness which is
so characteristic of everything psychic.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: Although Freudâ€™s book The Future of an Illusion dates from his later years, it gives the best possible account of his earlier views, which move within the confines of the outmoded rationalism and scientific materialism of the late nineteenth century.
text_raw:
Although Freudâ€™s
book The Future of an Illusion dates from his later years, it
gives the best possible account of his earlier views, which
move within the confines of the outmoded rationalism and
scientific materialism of the late nineteenth century.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: As might be expected, my book, born under such conditions, consisted of larger or smaller fragments which I could only string together in an unsatisfying manner.
text_raw:
As might be expected, my book, born under such conditions,
consisted of larger or smaller fragments which I could only
string together in an unsatisfying manner.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: It was an attempt, only partially successful, to create a wider setting for medical psychology and to bring the whole of the psychic phenomenon within its purview.
text_raw:
It was an attempt,
only partially successful, to create a wider setting for medical
psychology and to bring the whole of the psychic
phenomenon within its purview.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: One of my principal aims was to free medical psychology from the subjective and personalistic bias that characterized its outlook at that time, and to make it possible to understand the unconscious as an objective and collective psyche.
text_raw:
One of my principal aims
was to free medical psychology from the subjective and
personalistic bias that characterized its outlook at that time,
and to make it possible to understand the unconscious as an
objective and collective psyche.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: The personalism in the views of Freud and Adler that went hand in hand with the individualism of the nineteenth century failed to satisfy me because, except in the case of instinctive dynamisms (which actually have too little place in Adler), it left no room for objective, impersonal facts.
text_raw:
The personalism in the views
of Freud and Adler that went hand in hand with the
individualism of the nineteenth century failed to satisfy me
because, except in the case of instinctive dynamisms (which
actually have too little place in Adler), it left no room for
objective, impersonal facts.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: Freud, accordingly, could see no objective justification for my attempt, but suspected personal motives.
text_raw:
Freud, accordingly, could see no
objective justification for my attempt, but suspected personal
motives.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: Thus this book became a landmark, set up on the spot where two ways divided.
text_raw:
Thus this book became a landmark, set up on the spot where
two ways divided.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: Because of its imperfections and its incompleteness it laid down the programme to be followed for the next few decades of my life.
text_raw:
Because of its imperfections and its
incompleteness it laid down the programme to be followed
for the next few decades of my life.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: Hardly had I finished the manuscript when it struck me what it means to live with a myth, and what it means to live without one.
text_raw:
Hardly had I finished the
manuscript when it struck me what it means to live with a
myth, and what it means to live without one.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: Myth, says a Church Father, is â€œwhat is believed always, everywhere, by everybodyâ€; hence the man who thinks he can live without
text_raw:
Myth, says a
Church Father, is â€œwhat is believed always, everywhere, by
everybodyâ€; hence the man who thinks he can live without

chapter_title: Frontmatter
Frontmatter
text: myth, or outside it, is an exception.
text_raw: myth, or outside it, is an exception.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: He is like one uprooted, having no true link either with the past, or with the ancestral life which continues within him, or yet with contemporary human society.
text_raw:
He is like one uprooted,
having no true link either with the past, or with the ancestral
life which continues within him, or yet with contemporary
human society.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: He does not live in a house like other men, does not eat and drink like other men, but lives a life of his own, sunk in a subjective mania of his own devising, which he believes to be the newly discovered truth.
text_raw:
He does not live in a house like other men,
does not eat and drink like other men, but lives a life of his
own, sunk in a subjective mania of his own devising, which
he believes to be the newly discovered truth.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: This plaything of his reason never grips his vitals.
text_raw:
This plaything
of his reason never grips his vitals.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: It may occasionally lie heavy on his stomach, for that organ is apt to reject the products of reason as indigestible.
text_raw:
It may occasionally lie
heavy on his stomach, for that organ is apt to reject the
products of reason as indigestible.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: The psyche is not of today; its ancestry goes back many millions of years.
text_raw:
The psyche is not of today;
its ancestry goes back many millions of years.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: Individual consciousness is only the flower and the fruit of a season, sprung from the perennial rhizome beneath the earth; and it would find itself in better accord with the truth if it took the existence of the rhizome into its calculations.
text_raw:
Individual
consciousness is only the flower and the fruit of a season,
sprung from the perennial rhizome beneath the earth; and it
would find itself in better accord with the truth if it took the
existence of the rhizome into its calculations.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: For the root matter is the mother of all things.
text_raw:
For the root
matter is the mother of all things.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: So I suspected that myth had a meaning which I was sure to miss if I lived outside it in the haze of my own speculations.
text_raw:
So I suspected that myth had a meaning which I was sure to
